summary: Closed the open item by source and corrected the account where that changes it. The trace shows why the new leader never decides its own entry in the shift construction: a follower holds replicated entries in its batch and replies `Accepted` only when the batch flushes, which happens either when the batch fills or on the flush-batch logical clock (`flush_batch_tick_timeout`, 100 ticks here) — so with batch_size 3 a single replicated entry waits 100 actor ticks, and at a 1000 ms tick that exceeds the run, leaving the new leader without a write quorum and the origin's re-synchronisation carrying decided index 0. That also explains the phase split across the retained runs: at 100 ms the flush fires after about ten seconds, inside the run, which is exactly the group that reported decided index 1 and the new leader's call resolving. The correction I had to make is that my measured band is confounded with this flush deadline, because the tick period scales the deadline as well as the resolution window, and the two groups divide exactly along whether that deadline fell inside the run — so the tick period is no longer established as the condition separating the holding from the violating runs, even though the caller-visible violation itself stands and is reproduced. I recorded the deferral mechanism as knowledge with its source anchors, rewrote the interpretation's rationale, counterevidence and limitations around it, and set the discriminator to a construction that decouples the two (batch_size 1 at the origin with a small flush timeout, or a follower whose batch is filled so the flush is immediate). No execution was requested this turn (validation reports execution_requested false).
